administration.vendor: IEA / TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center

design.notes: Matrix (booklet) item sampling assumed from the TIMSS parent; participating countries are store sub-jurisdictions. Both A0.2 TODOs are closed by the maintainer sign-off of 2026-09-02. The seventh character of a PV name is the wave (1 = 2023, 2 = 2024) and the eighth is the imputation index, so the 2024 wave is ASMMAT21-ASMMAT25 (G5) and BSMMAT21-BSMMAT25 (G9) - deliberately not the 2023 G4/G8 ASMMAT/BSMMAT. Linked-sample weight is TOTWGT; there is no longitudinal-specific weight. Verified against Fishbein, Taneva & Kowolik (2026), TIMSS 2023 Longitudinal User Guide, Ch. 2 pp. 51-52 (Exhibit 2.5 and the naming rules) and pp. 64-66 (Exhibit 2.10).

enrollment.note: Follow-up of TIMSS 2023 grade 4 (now 5) and grade 8 (now 9). Scores are on the TIMSS 2023 mathematics scale; there is no separate TIMSS-L standard setting.

MATHEMATICS.notes: Labels copied from timss-intl-2023 for the inherited International Benchmarks. IEA did not set separate TIMSS-L cut scores. proficient_from is the same placeholder as the 2023 record, not an IEA designation.

cutscores_provenance: No separate TIMSS-L cut scores. IEA TIMSS-L Progress Report (GA64, 2023): learning gains are measured on the TIMSS achievement scales; the 2023 grade 4/8 cohort is reassessed as grade 5/9 in 2024. MATHEMATICS International Benchmarks therefore inherit from timss-intl-2023 (Low 400 / Intermediate 475 / High 550 / Advanced 625; constant since TIMSS 2003). cutscores / cutscores_source are omitted so a consumer must resolve the linked administration rather than read a duplicated vector here.
notes: First-pass scope is MATHEMATICS. Carries no cut scores of its own: it inherits the TIMSS international benchmarks from timss-intl-2023. Reviewed rather than verified for that reason - there is no cut-score claim here to confirm against a citation.
